objections.claim: The merge controller’s startup proof is inoperable under its own fixed credential manifest. E1 requires the controller itself to read classic branch protection (`required_status_checks.strict`) and complete bypass-actor data for every effective ruleset, refusing when visibility is unavailable. Section 5(e) simultaneously limits that credential to `contents:write + pull_requests:write + checks:read` and explicitly grants no administration permission. GitHub requires `Administration:read` to get branch protection, while ruleset `bypass_actors` are returned only to callers with write access to the ruleset. [GitHub branch-protection API](https://docs.github.com/en/enterprise-cloud@latest/rest/branches/branch-protection) and [GitHub rulesets API](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/repos/rules). Consequently, the stated compliant configuration necessarily fails `bypass-visibility-unavailable`/`unsafe-merge-environment` before every merge; adding administration access would contradict the exact least-privilege custody manifest. Separate the privileged configuration attestation from the merge credential, or reconcile the credential/trust design, with a regression exercising the real permission-limited responses.
